dedupe_keys.name: us counties overlap of broadband gaps and scarce health facilities healthcare unplugged

description: This case study asks whether US counties with poor broadband internet, where telemedicine is harder to use, are also the counties with fewest health facilities. The authors, from Harvard, Stanford, Oxford, Memorial Sloan Kettering and other institutions, combined for 3,133 counties the density of outpatient care centres, diagnostic laboratories and nursing and residential care facilities from the 2017 National Neighborhood Data Archive, broadband access from the 2022 FCC Mapping Broadband Health in America data, split at the median of 9.8 percent of households without broadband, urbanicity, and covariates from the 2022 American Community Survey. They used t-tests, multivariable regression and heat maps. The article was published in PLOS Digital Health in July 2026 and is free to read online under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is national, by county. Caveats: the analysis is cross-sectional and ecological, and facility data are from 2017. Maps show that areas with few health facilities, notably the Great Plains and the Southwest, overlap with low broadband coverage, and counties with low broadband access had fewer outpatient care centres (10.46 against 11.91 per 100,000 residents) and diagnostic laboratories (1.91 against 3.95 per 100,000). Simulation uses: county-level dependency of health access on telecom coverage for interdependency and access models. Related records: the NaNDA broadband data (data-nanda-broadband-internet-by-tract) is one of its inputs.
